Counsel for Respondent :- G.A.,Gaurav Saxena,Jushi Saxena,Lalla Chauhan,Neeraj Kumar Sax
Hon'ble Ramesh Sinha,J.
Hon'ble Narendra Kumar Johari,J.
Supplementary affidavit filed on behalf of the petitioners is taken on record.

Heard Sri Ashish Shukla, learned counsel for the petitioners, Sri Aditya Singh holding brief of Sri Neeraj Kumar Saxena, learned counsel for the private respondent and learned Additional Government Advocate for the State and perused the record.

By means of the present petition, the petitioners have prayed for quashing of the impugned FIR dated 11.01.2022 as FIR No. 0025 of 2022, under Sections 498A/323/504/506/354 IPC and Sections 3 and 4 of the Dowry Prohibition Act, Police Station Madiyaon, District Lucknow North,
contained as Annexure no. 1 to this writ petition with a further prayer to direct the respondents not to arrest the petitioners in pursuance of impugned FIR.

sentences.text: 1 Learned counsel for the petitioners submits that the dispute between petitioner no. 1 and respondent no. 3 is matrimonial one but the compromise has been arrived between the petitioners and private respondent no. 3.
The fact of the compromise has not been disputed by learned counsel for the private respondent no. 3.

It has further been stated by learned counsel for the petitioner that an application under Section 13-B of the Hindu Marriage Act has been filed and mutual compromise has been taken place between the parties before the family court No. 4, Lucknow on 13.03.2023.
A copy of the same has been filed as Annexure no. 2 to the supplementary affidavit.

Placing reliance upon the judgments of the Apex Court in Manoj Sharma Vs. State : (2008) 16 SCC 1,
B.S. Joshi Vs. State of Haryana and others : 2003 (4) SCC 675, Gian Singh Vs. State of Punjab and another : (2012) 10 SCC 303 and Narinder Singh and others Vs. State of Punjab and another :
(2014) 6 SCC 466, learned Counsel for the petitioners has submitted that the petitioner no. 1 and respondent no. 3 are the husband and wife and mutual compromise has been taken place between the parties before the family court No. 4, Lucknow on 13.03.2023.

sentences.text: In these backdrops, his submission is that in view of the aforesaid compromise, no fruitful purpose would be served if the prosecution is allowed to go on.
Learned Counsel for respondent no.3 could not dispute the aforesaid facts.

Having heard learned Counsel for the parties and considering the facts and circumstances of the case, it is apparent that dispute between petitioners and private respondent no. 3 has been compromised.

The fact of the compromise has not been disputed by learned counsel for the private respondent no. 3 and an application under Section 13-B of the Hindu Marriage Act has been filed and mutual compromise has been taken place between the parties before the family court No. 4,
Lucknow on 13.03.2023.

Therefore, in view of the judgments of the Apex Court in Manoj Sharma (supra), B.S. Joshi (supra), Gian Singh and Narinder Singh (supra), relied by the learned Counsel for the petitioners, we are of the view that this Court in exercise of its inherent power under Article 226 of the Constitution of India can quash the FIR as the dispute has been amicably settled between the parties by means of compromise dated 12.09.2022.
In view of the aforesaid, the writ petition is allowed.

The impugned FIR dated 11.01.2022, FIR No.
0025 of 2022, under Sections 498A/323/504/506/354 IPC and Sections 3 and 4 of the Dowry Prohibition Act, Police Station Madiyaon, District Lucknow North, contained as Annexure no. 1 to this writ petition is hereby quashed.
[Narendra Kumar Johari,J.] [Ramesh Sinha,J.]
